A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPIO framework and retain matching core equations and experiments. Text, tables, figures, and appendices are readable; the substantial reformatting and expanded material do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Kaggle and OpenML benchmark results and plan-ranking, ensemble-size, and module-removal ablations in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark and ablation results, additional dataset evaluations, failure and token-use analyses, and an expert evaluation in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The four-module code-generation and sequential-planning procedure, LLM selection, and classification/regression ensembling remain unchanged, including equations 1–12. Revised candidate counts configure the existing procedure rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original 12 datasets and adds rainfall classification, backpack-price regression, and podcast-listening-time regression in Appendix A. It also adds subjective pipeline evaluation involving 10 AI practitioners or graduate-level participants.

E2.justification: V1 already evaluates ZeroShot, CoT, Agent K, AutoKaggle, and Data Interpreter. V2 adds OpenHands and AIDE comparisons for GPT-4o and Claude, plus public Kaggle human-expert reference scores. OpenHands and AIDE are explicitly unavailable for LLaMA3-8B.

E3.justification: V2 adds LLaMA3-8B and changes the reported maximum candidate plans per module from three to two. OpenML regression reporting changes from MSE to RMSE, and ablation summaries switch from rank frequencies and weighted ranks to ACC/ROC and RMSE. New analyses introduce retry thresholds, embedding/PCA procedures, and Likert and forced-choice evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: The three existing ablation questions are retained with revised reporting and an additional backend. V2 adds a pretraining-exposure check using recent datasets, execution-failure analyses, token-cost trade-offs, plan-diversity analyses, expert agreement testing, and a detailed Monsters pipeline case study.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates and rank frequencies without statistical testing. V2 introduces benchmark significance markers, paired t-tests with Holm–Bonferroni correction, and mean/standard-deviation reporting for expert ratings (Tables 1, 3, and 10). Benchmark repetition counts, seeds, and the pairing underlying benchmark tests remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Many reported scores change: GPT-4o SPIO-E Titanic accuracy changes from 0.8062 to 0.7871 under revised planning settings, so this is not an established same-setting deterioration. V2 adds extensive comparator, backend, dataset, expert, failure, and cost results and replaces rank-frequency ablation entries. Several OpenML numerical changes are simply MSE-to-RMSE conversions.

T1.justification: The method mathematics in equations 1–12 is retained. V1's explicit weighted average-rank definition in equation 13 is removed, while v2 defines FR@K as a failure proportion. These are limited definition changes; neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains sequential multi-path planning with selective and ensemble variants. The headline average improvement changes from 11% in v1's conclusion to 5.6% in v2's abstract and conclusion, while the broader superiority and robustness claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds explicit limitations concerning global optimality and sensitivity to the LLM backend, prompt context, and stochastic generation. It also introduces interpretations concerning pretraining exposure, failure recovery, token efficiency, expert agreement, and semantic diversity, including qualifications about interpreting PCA projections.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies top_p=1.0, max_tokens=4096, a module-specific library whitelist, plan-logging practices, and embedding details. It supplies sources for the added datasets. Existing prompt templates largely move from Appendix A to Appendix F, with candidate-count revisions; these disclosures do not establish additional underlying method changes.

R1.justification: The AutoML background and central positioning are retained. V2 extends related work with OpenHands, AIDE, recent surveys, blackboard-based discovery, and agent benchmarks, adding discussion of execution budgets and plan traceability. Data Interpreter's 2024-to-2025 citation change refers to the same work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, discussion, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. V2 adds a Preliminaries subsection, a dedicated qualitative-study section and limitations passage, and extensively reorganizes the appendices while relocating existing prompts and case studies.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, replaces the overview figures, consolidates benchmark and ablation tables, and adds failure, cost, diversity, and expert-evaluation displays. Prompts become numbered tables. Existing case-study diagrams are reformatted, with the SPIO-E example revised from three final pipelines to two.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, stronger comparators, recent datasets, a smaller LLM, practical reliability/cost analyses, and explicit limitations make v2's validation more informative. However, benchmark significance claims lack replication and pairing details, and some conclusions conflict with the new evidence: Table 2 contains an exception to two-plan ensemble superiority, and Table 7 reports Claude SPIO-S FR@3=0.08 despite the prose claiming zero. These gaps limit the overall gain in confidence.
